questions.q: What question has Store Operations always needed this report page to answer?
options: How are my stores doing, day to day -- a trend question at the store level
Which product categories are driving sales across the chain
How does this store compare to every other store side by side
What percentage of transactions are returns or refunds
questions.explain: Store Ops' question has never changed: a day-to-day, store-level trend of how sales are moving, which gold.daily_sales_summary is built at exactly the right grain to answer.

questions.q: Why is a line chart used for total_sales by sale_date instead of a bar chart?
options: A line makes direction and change over time immediately visible, which is what the trend question needs
Bar charts cannot plot a date field on the x-axis
Line charts load faster in Power BI than bar charts
Power BI does not support bar charts for currency values
questions.explain: The underlying question is about direction and change over time, which a line visually communicates more directly than a bar chart of daily totals.

questions.q: Why does store_id belong on a slicer rather than being baked into the chart as a fixed filter?
options: A slicer lets the same chart answer the question for whichever store (or stores) someone wants to check, without separate pages per store
gold.daily_sales_summary does not contain a store_id column
Slicers are required by Power BI for every numeric field
Baking store_id into the chart would violate the Gold table's schema
questions.explain: Store Ops checks different stores at different times; a slicer keeps one page and one chart flexible instead of requiring a separate chart or page per store.

questions.q: What question does the total_transactions callout answer that the trend line alone cannot?
options: Whether the sales total reflects a few large transactions or a lot of normal ones
Which category is contributing the most to total sales
Whether the data has fully reconciled between Gold tables
How many stores exist in the chain
questions.explain: Sales dollars and transaction count can tell different stories; the callout keeps transaction volume visible at a glance alongside the sales trend.

questions.q: Why would adding a category breakdown to this specific page be the wrong move, even though the data exists?
options: Store Ops' actual question is a store-level day-to-day trend, not a category question -- that belongs to the Regional Manager's page on a different Gold table
gold.daily_sales_summary technically has no sale_date column
Category breakdowns are only possible in DirectQuery mode
Adding another visual would exceed Power BI's per-page visual limit
questions.explain: A report page should answer the question actually asked. The category question is a different stakeholder's ask, answered by gold.category_breakdown on the next lesson's page, not by overloading this one.
